competencies.text: Describe how the greenhouse effect regulates Earth's temperature.

days.title: The Greenhouse Effect
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to explain how the greenhouse effect works, identify the major greenhouse gases, distinguish the natural greenhouse effect from the enhanced greenhouse effect, and describe Earth's energy balance.

🌡️ Earth's Energy Balance

Earth receives energy from the Sun and radiates energy back to space. In a balanced system, the amount in equals the amount out — keeping Earth's average temperature stable at about 15°C.

Earth's energy balance follows three main paths when sunlight arrives:

  1. ~30% is reflected back to space by clouds, ice, and bright surfaces (called albedo).
  2. ~20% is absorbed by the atmosphere (ozone, water vapor, clouds).
  3. ~50% is absorbed by Earth's surface (land and oceans), warming the planet.

The absorbed energy is later radiated back as infrared (IR) radiation — heat.

🌿 What Is the Greenhouse Effect?

The greenhouse effect is the process by which certain gases in the atmosphere trap some of the infrared radiation (heat) that Earth emits, keeping the planet warm enough for life.

Sunlight in → Earth warms → IR emitted → GHGs absorb IR → Re-emit in all directions → Some escapes, some returns → Earth stays warm

🔬 The Major Greenhouse Gases

GasFormulaMain SourceGlobal Warming Potential (GWP)
Water vaporH₂OEvaporation from oceans, lakes— (most abundant, natural)
Carbon dioxideCO₂Fossil fuels, deforestation, respiration1 (reference)
MethaneCH₄Livestock, rice paddies, landfills~28× CO₂
Nitrous oxideN₂OFertilizers, industrial processes~265× CO₂
OzoneO₃Natural + pollution (tropospheric)Varies
Fluorinated gases (CFCs, HFCs)VariousRefrigerants, aerosolsHundreds to thousands × CO₂

🌍 Natural vs. Enhanced Greenhouse Effect

TypeWhat It IsEffect
Natural greenhouse effectGreenhouse gases that occur naturally keep Earth ~33°C warmer than it would be without themEnables life — without it Earth's average would be −18°C
Enhanced greenhouse effectHuman activities add extra GHGs (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O) that increase the trapping of heatGlobal warming; climate change; sea-level rise; extreme weather

Key idea: The natural greenhouse effect is good and necessary. The enhanced greenhouse effect (from human activity) is what causes climate change.

☀️ The Electromagnetic Spectrum Connection

Why doesn't sunlight just pass through GHGs too?

  • Sunlight arrives as visible light (short wavelength, high energy). GHGs do not absorb visible light well.
  • Earth's heat is emitted as infrared radiation (long wavelength, lower energy). GHGs do absorb IR.

This is the physics behind the greenhouse effect — molecules like CO₂ and H₂O have chemical bonds that vibrate at IR frequencies.

🌡️ Why 15°C Is Just Right

Earth's average surface temperature is 15°C. Compare with:

  • Venus (464°C) — runaway greenhouse effect with 96% CO₂
  • Mars (−63°C) — very thin atmosphere, weak greenhouse effect
  • Earth without greenhouse effect (−18°C) — too cold for most life

🇵🇭 Why This Matters for the Philippines

  • The Philippines contributes only 0.3% of global CO₂ emissions — but is among the most vulnerable to climate impacts.
  • Warmer oceans fuel stronger typhoons (like Yolanda/Haiyan in 2013, Odette/Rai in 2021).
  • Rising sea levels threaten coastal barangays and freshwater supplies.

📌 Quick Check

  • What would Earth's average temperature be without the greenhouse effect? (Answer: −18°C)
  • Which gas traps the most heat per molecule? (Answer: fluorinated gases, then N₂O, CH₄, CO₂)
  • What kind of radiation do greenhouse gases absorb? (Answer: infrared — heat)

days.title: Match Game — Greenhouse Gases
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each concept or gas to its correct description or source. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Gases trap infrared radiation, warming Earth's surface
Released by fossil fuels and deforestation; reference GWP = 1
Released by livestock, rice paddies, and landfills; ~28× CO₂ GWP
Extra GHGs from human activity that amplify warming
Fraction of sunlight reflected by clouds, ice, and bright surfaces
Type of radiation Earth emits as heat — absorbed by GHGs

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Earth's Thermostat
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: ☀️ Sunlight passes through Earth's atmosphere but heat doesn't easily escape. Why?

choices.label: A) Sunlight is visible light (short wavelength) and GHGs don't absorb it well; heat is infrared (long wavelength) and GHGs absorb it
C) Sunlight is stronger than heat
D) Earth's gravity holds heat in place

scenario.text: 🥩 A livestock farm has many cows producing methane. How does this contribute to climate change?

choices.label: A) Methane is a greenhouse gas that is ~28× more potent than CO₂ at trapping heat
B) Cows eat all the plants
C) Cows use too much water

scenario.text: ❄️ Ice at the North and South Poles reflects sunlight. As ice melts due to warming, what happens to the greenhouse effect?

choices.label: A) Less ice → less reflection → more heat absorbed → more warming (a positive feedback loop)

scenario.text: 🌫️ Without the natural greenhouse effect, what would Earth's average temperature be?

choices.label: A) About −18°C — too cold for most life

scenario.text: 🇵🇭 The Philippines contributes only 0.3% of global CO₂ emissions but faces strong climate impacts. Why?

choices.label: A) It's an archipelago in the typhoon belt with coastal communities vulnerable to sea-level rise and storms
B) It has the largest population
C) It burns the most fossil fuels
D) It has no greenhouse gases

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Atmosphere Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Atmosphere Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: What would Earth's average temperature be WITHOUT the natural greenhouse effect?
Which greenhouse gas is the MOST abundant naturally in Earth's atmosphere?
What kind of radiation do greenhouse gases absorb?
Which gas has the HIGHEST global warming potential per molecule?
The ENHANCED greenhouse effect is caused by:

choices.label: A) Human activities that add extra greenhouse gases
